key_insight: A self-supervised functional autoencoder learns a reusable, task-agnostic latent space, separating function representation from neural operator training.
engineering_relevance: For solid-mechanics surrogates, frozen representations can reduce operator-training memory and time while supporting fields on arbitrary point clouds.
method: Pre-train on analytic functions synthesized without solvers or labels.
Freeze encoder and decoder, then train operators on cached embeddings.
Use representations exactly equivariant to translation, dilation, and amplitude.
evidence_signal: Across 28 tasks spanning solid mechanics and other PDE domains, the abstract reports accuracy that can exceed state-of-the-art end-to-end models, with up to an order-of-magnitude higher throughput.
watch_item: Transfer to a specific engineering application still requires validation; aggregate results do not establish accuracy for every geometry, material law, or loading regime.
paper_title: Self-Supervised Learning of Universal Latent Spaces for Operator Learning
